All clinical data converge with high specificity and diagnostic certainty on **Hirschsprung disease (HD)** in this 2-day-old male infant. The presentation is classic: *bilious vomiting since birth*, *failure to pass meconium*, *abdominal distension*, *decreased bowel sounds*, and *palpable dilated loops* — all indicating functional intestinal obstruction due to aganglionic colonic segment. - Clinical: 2-day-old male, bilious vomiting since birth, absolute failure to pass meconium, abdominal distension, discomfort, decreased bowel sounds, firm/tympanitic abdomen with palpable loops.
